subject: Private deployment: key lifecycle telemetry & emergency spiral plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <sec@noblehealth.com>, Acme Cloud Ops <ops@acmecloud.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment: key lifecycle telemetry & emergency spiral plan

Hi Jane / Acme team —

Following our recent kickoff, I want to align on two narrow but critical pieces for NobleHealth's Private deployment:

1) Key lifecycle telemetry matrix — what events we need emitted from the HSM/KMS and how long we retain that telemetry for audit.
2) An "emergency spiral" runbook — a clear, tested sequence (telemetry checks, policy toggle, cross-region failover, key rotation/eviction) when we need to rapidly isolate or rotate customer KEKs for compromise scenarios.

Attached are a draft runbook and a telemetry matrix (high-level). Can you review and confirm the following by EOD Tuesday?
- Minimum telemetry events required for your auditors (e.g., unseal/seal, key-wrap ops, partition attach/detach, admin ACL changes).
- Acceptable retention window for telemetry and whether scrubbed copies are allowable for cross-team incident reviews.
- Who on your side can sign emergency authorization (name + email) for an accelerated spiral.

Internally, Laura and Aditya are listed to own the architecture details and the HSM partitioning plan. Marcus is on standby for test plan coordination.

Thanks — looking to lock this down so we can schedule the attestation window.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: spiral-runbook-v1.pdf (draft), kms-telemetry-matrix.xlsx (matrix), attestation-checklist.docx

From: Jane Doe <sec@noblehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Cloud Ops <ops@acmecloud.io>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: key lifecycle telemetry & emergency spiral plan

Soojin —

Appreciate the clear ask. Initial notes from NobleHealth Security:
- Minimum telemetry: unseal, seal, admin policy changes, key-wrap/unwrap ops (including caller identity), failed auth attempts, partition attach/detach. We also want time-series counters for key usage (per-key, per-tenant aggregate).
- Retention: auditors require 2 years for high-fidelity telemetry; for operational use, 90 days hot, 455 days cold archived. We will sign an NDA addendum for limited-copy archives for joint incident reviews.
- Emergency authorization: I can sign for initial tests; escalation list will include our CISO (ciso@noblehealth.com) and head of infrastructure (infra-lead@noblehealth.com).

Question: can Redwood support a dual-provision approach where the KEK is wrapped by an on-prem HSM and a backup wrapped key is held in a separate, geo-isolated vault (cold escrow)? That impacts the spiral path.

Thanks — Jane
Jane Doe
Director, Security Engineering
NobleHealth

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jane Doe <sec@noblehealth.com>, Acme Cloud Ops <ops@acmecloud.io>
Date: Sun, 15 Jan 2028 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: key lifecycle telemetry & emergency spiral plan

Thanks Jane — quick internal proposals below (subject to HSM vendor confirmations):

- Rotation cadence: KEK (customer master) rotate annually by default; automated quarterly wrap-rotation for ephemeral wrapping keys that protect tenant session keys. Emergency rotation path must complete within 6 hours for all active tenants when authorized.
- Dual-provision escrow: we propose split custody for the cold-escrow key: encrypted shard A stored in NobleHealth-managed HSM, shard B stored in Redwood cold escrow (sequestered HSM in a different region). Reconstruction requires 2/2 for emergency.
- Telemetry retention plan: 90d hot in infra metrics (Grafana/Prometheus), 455d archived to immutable storage with signed manifests. Access to archived telemetry is via documented process and joint authorization.

Action items for Monday: confirm whether NobleHealth wants 2/2 or 2/3 split custody, and whether the escrow should be under a third-party custodian (VaultCloud suggested).

Link: proposal + matrix https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1KmsTelemetryMatrix

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal Architect, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jane Doe <sec@noblehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jan 2028 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: key lifecycle telemetry & emergency spiral plan

On Sun, Jan 15, 2028 at 1:20 PM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Dual-provision escrow: we propose split custody for the cold-escrow key: encrypted shard A stored in NobleHealth-managed HSM, shard B stored in Redwood cold escrow (sequestered HSM in a different region). Reconstruction requires 2/2 for emergency.

Couple of clarifications from infra perspective:
- HSM partitioning: we'll allocate a dedicated partition per tenant for KEKs and a platform partition for ephemeral wrapping keys. Partition attach/detach telemetry must include partition id and operator identity.
- KEK derivation: prefer HKDF-SHA256 with per-tenant salt derived from tenant ID and creation timestamp. We should avoid raw KEK export; only wrapped keys leave the HSM boundary.
- Emergency spiral: sequence I propose — (1) Validate telemetry anomalies (automated detection rule), (2) Lock admin plane (ACL freeze), (3) Revoke active wrapping keys, (4) Promote cold escrow shards to initiate a controlled rewrap, (5) Rotate routing policies to fallback model variant. Documented timers and rollback windows required.

I'll add a concise state machine diagram to the runbook. Marcus, can you own test orchestration?

— Aditya
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Acme Cloud Ops <ops@acmecloud.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jane Doe <sec@noblehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jan 2028 10:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: key lifecycle telemetry & emergency spiral plan

Soojin / team —

We can support on-site attestation and a crossconnect for the privileged HSM link. A couple of operational notes:
- Network: we require a dedicated VPC peering with MACsec-capable crossconnect; ensure the HSM control plane is on an isolated mgmt subnet.
- Telemetry retention: we support the 90d hot / 455d cold plan. However, for archived telemetry we need explicit retention class and legal hold API hooks (we can expose a signed manifest + signed timestamp for any pulled archive).
- Scrubbing: we need to agree on a redaction policy for PII in metadata; certain token prefixes will be allowed for correlation only.

We can schedule an attestation window for the week of Jan 29. Please provide the finalized runbook and the emergency authorization roster before then.

— Acme Cloud Ops (on behalf of Marcus Lin)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
